label: Superlatives
outcome: Lo studente identifica o presenta l'elemento con il grado massimo o minimo di una qualità dentro un gruppo di almeno tre, usando the + -est, the most e best/worst con spelling corretto.
must_master: use a superlative when comparing one member with a group of three or more
selected short CVC adjectives with doubled final consonant + -est
irregular the best and the worst
simple in/of group context after a superlative

scope_boundary.comparatives: Comparatives are a prerequisite, not a second target. Do not turn the lesson into comparative-vs-superlative drills except where group meaning is needed to choose correctly.
scope_boundary.advanced_superlatives: Do not teach least, one of the..., by far, ever + present perfect, or advanced emphasis.
scope_boundary.articles: Teach the article the as part of the superlative pattern only; broader article use belongs to the articles topic.
scope_boundary.prepositions: Use simple in/of group phrases but do not expand into a general prepositions lesson.

italian_learner_risks.example_wrong: Marta is tallest student in the class.
italian_learner_risks.target: Marta is the tallest student in the class.

italian_learner_risks.risk: using most with a short -est form
italian_learner_risks.example_wrong: This is the most cheapest option.

italian_learner_risks.risk: using most with a short adjective instead of -est
italian_learner_risks.example_wrong: It is the most small room.

italian_learner_risks.risk: using a superlative for a comparison of only two items
italian_learner_risks.example_wrong: Of the two routes, this is the shortest.
italian_learner_risks.target: Of the two routes, this is the shorter one.

context_bank: rooms or buildings in a town

requirements: teach the + -est, -iest, doubled consonant, the most, best/worst
mix group meaning, form, spelling and irregulars
include a connected decision or survey context
increase autonomy from recognition to production
no labels that reveal the required form
approximately 60 percent standard and 40 percent challenge

quality_rejections: questions that can be answered without a group or clear maximum/minimum meaning
systematic mixing with comparatives as a second grammar target
more than two consecutive isolated adjective-to-superlative conversions
the most + short adjective used in answer keys where -est is expected
missing the in standard noun-phrase superlatives
ambiguous groups where the reference set is not clear
advanced constructions outside the Year 1 target
difficulty created by uncommon adjectives rather than grammar decisions
